chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us who said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us who said: He (Muhammad) narrated to me Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khishab, from Al-Hasan ibn Ishaq al-Tamimi, from Al-Hasan ibn Akhi al-Dabbi, from Abdullah ibn Sin'an who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

The sun sets (its shadow lengthens) in the middle of Haziran (June) by half a foot, and in the middle of Tammuz (July) by one and a half feet, and in the middle of Ab (August) by two and a half feet, and in the middle of Elul (September) by three and a half feet, and in the middle of Tishri al-Awwal (October) by five and a half feet, and in the middle of Tishri al-Akhir (November) by seven and a half feet, and in the middle of Kanun al-Awwal (December) by nine and a half feet, and in the middle of Kanun al-Akhir (January) by seven and a half feet, and in the middle of Shabat (February) by five feet and a half, and in the middle of Adar (March) by three and a half feet, and in the middle of Nisan (April) by two and a half feet, and in the middle of Ayar (May) by one and a half feet, and in the middle of Haziran (June) by half a foot.

key_terms.تَزُولُ الشَّمْسُ: The setting of the sun / lengthening of the shadow at noon

ai.seo_question: What is the length of the noon shadow in each month according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) precise measurements of the sun's shadow at noon, linking specific months to distinct shadow lengths to demonstrate the sun's declination. This narration serves as a practical astronomical guide for Muslims to determine the direction of the Qibla and the timing of prayers by observing natural signs, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on utilizing reason and observation of creation. The detailed monthly breakdown highlights the systematic order (*nizam*) of the cosmos as a sign of divine wisdom.
